remoteRow.chooseOrCreateFolderDialogTitle: Choose or create a local folder
remoteRow.mountAction: Mount: connect this remote as a local folder
remoteRow.conflictMessage: This remote already has {active} active. Turning on {target} will disable {active}.
remoteRow.winFspInstallerStarted: The WinFsp installer started in a separate window: finish it, then come back here and try mounting again.
remoteRow.propagateDeletionsOnHint: On: files removed from the source are also removed from the destination on every sync.
remoteRow.propagateDeletionsOffHint: Off (recommended): the destination only accumulates copies — nothing is ever deleted automatically, even if it disappears from the source.
remoteRow.dryRunCheckbox: Dry-run mode: doesn't copy or delete anything, just shows what it would do
remoteRow.propagateDeletionsWarningIntro: You're about to turn on "Propagate deletions" for the backup of {remote}.
remoteRow.propagateDeletionsWarningOnBody: on every sync, files removed (or no longer present) in the source will also be removed from the destination — the destination becomes an exact mirror of the source. If the source turns out empty or temporarily unreachable (e.g. an external disk got disconnected), you risk emptying the destination.
remoteRow.propagateDeletionsWarningOffTitle: If you don't turn it on:
remoteRow.propagateDeletionsWarningOffBody: files arrive and get updated in the destination, but nothing is ever deleted automatically, even if it disappears from the source — the destination can only accumulate, never lose data through an automatic sync.
remoteRow.bisyncFirstRunHint: On the very first run, if a file with the same name but different content already exists on both sides, the more recently modified version is taken as the reference.
remoteRow.needsResyncHint: The next run will include a new resync (baseline).
remoteRow.noVersionLost: No version was lost: both were saved with a conflict suffix.
remoteRow.forceBisyncWarningIntro: rclone blocked this sync because it detected that too many files would be deleted relative to the total (protection against mass deletions) — check the log above to see which files would be affected before continuing.
remoteRow.forceBisyncWarningHint: If you proceed, the deletions will actually be applied on the other side. If the cause was a disconnected disk, a moved folder, or something similar, close this panel and fix that first before retrying.
remoteRow.noActiveService: No service active for this remote.
remoteRow.deleteConfirmQuestion: Do you really want to delete this remote?
remoteRow.alsoDeleted: The following will also be deleted:

newRemote.title: Add a remote
newRemote.subtitle: Choose the type of storage to connect.
newRemote.importCardDesc: Already have remotes configured with rclone? Import them instead of recreating them.
newRemote.s3CardDesc: Includes Cubbit, Wasabi, and other S3-compatible providers with a custom endpoint.
newRemote.driveCardDesc: Authorization in the browser. Google will retire the shared identity rclone has used so far during 2026 — at the next step you can already create your own.
newRemote.nextcloudCardDesc: Server address, username and password (or app password).
newRemote.webdavCardDesc: For any other service compatible with the WebDAV protocol.
newRemote.sftpCardDesc: Access to a server over SSH: host, username and password.
newRemote.webdavHostHint: Just the server address (the one you use in the browser), without https:// and without a path — we'll take care of the rest.
newRemote.nextcloud2faHint: If you have two-factor authentication enabled, this needs an "app password" generated from Settings → Security on Nextcloud/ownCloud, not your regular password.
newRemote.ownClientExplainer: Google will disable the shared identity rclone has used so far during 2026: from that point on, Google Drive will stop working for anyone without their own client. Creating one takes about 5 minutes on Google Cloud Console and is free. You can also skip this step for now — the shared identity still works — and do it later by recreating the remote.
newRemote.step2: Click "Select a project" in the top left: choose an existing one or click "New project" and give it a name, e.g. "Rclone".
newRemote.step3Before: "APIs & Services" → "Library": use the search filter at the top to find
newRemote.step4Before: "APIs & Services" → "Credentials" → "Configure consent screen" (if you haven't already): user type
newRemote.step4After: (Internal only if you have a Google Workspace account), app name, and support email.
newRemote.step5Before: In the "Data Access" section: add the scopes
newRemote.step6: Only if you chose External: in the "Audience" menu add your email address to the "test users" (the app stays "unverified": fine for personal use, but only the listed test users can access it), then publish it from there.
newRemote.step7Before: In the "Clients" menu: click "Create client", type
newRemote.step8: Copy the generated Client ID and Client Secret and paste them below.
newRemote.officialGuideLink: Official rclone guide, for more details
newRemote.clientIdSecretBothRequired: Both the Client ID and Client Secret are needed, not just one.
newRemote.oauthOpenedBrowser: The browser opened for authorization with {provider} — complete the sign-in there.
newRemote.oauthOpenLinkManually: Didn't open automatically? Open the link
newRemote.endpointLabel: Endpoint (required for almost all providers except AWS)
newRemote.bucketRetryLabel: Bucket (enter it if your S3 key only has access to one bucket, then retry)
newRemote.advancedCardDesc: Can't find your service? Follow the same step-by-step flow as 'rclone config', through a graphical interface instead of the terminal.

advancedRemote.advancedPromptTitle: Do you also want to configure advanced options?
advancedRemote.advancedPromptHint: There are {count}, almost never needed: the defaults work fine for most users.

editRemote.title: Edit {remote}
editRemote.driveSharedWarningBefore: This Google Drive remote still uses rclone's shared identity, which
editRemote.driveSharedWarningAfter: — from that point it will stop working. To keep using it you need your own Google client, free and quick to create. Remotes authorized via browser can't be edited from here yet: to switch to your own client, delete this remote from the home screen and recreate it with the same name («{remote}») from "Add remote" → Google Drive, this time filling in "Use your own Google client". Mounts, backups, and syncs linked to this name stay valid — no need to recreate them.
editRemote.driveOwnClientOk: This Google Drive remote already uses your own Google client, and is not affected by Google's planned retirement of rclone's shared identity during 2026.
editRemote.oauthNotEditable: The parameters of remotes authorized via browser (Dropbox, OneDrive) can't be edited from here yet, only the name. If you need to change account, delete this remote from the previous page and recreate it.
editRemote.leaveEmptyToKeep: leave empty to keep it unchanged
